links.comparator_used: Existing scheduling practices: originally scheduled duration, historical averages, and Epic's CDE tool (user-adjusted and vendor-recommended configurations)
links.outcome: Surgical case duration estimation accuracy (MAE, bias, proportion within ±30 min or ±10%)
links.effect: Baseline scheduling: MAE 35.3 min, MSE bias -31 min, f30min 0.52, f10% 0.09. Standardized workflow with vendor-recommended Epic settings: MAE 20.1 min, f30min 0.81, f10% 0.37. ORchestra ML model: MAE 19.8 min, bias +1.2 min, fewer overscheduling outliers.
links.tradeoff: Most of the gain came from workflow standardization (consistent prep/wrap time inclusion, vendor-recommended Epic settings), which alone approached ML-level accuracy. The ML model added only a small further MAE reduction (20.1 to 19.8 min), with the largest gains in high-variability services.
links.quote: The ORchestra ML model further reduced error (MAE = 19.8 min), eliminated systematic bias (+1.2 min), and decreased overscheduling outliers, with the largest gains observed in high-variability services.

design_hint: workflow standardization and vendor-recommended software configuration before ML tool use
